html:
The leader of the democracy movement in Burma, winner of the Nobel Peace Prize in 1991, who spent about fifteen years under house arrest and later led the country's government.

She is the daughter of Aung San, the father of Burmese independence, who was killed when she was two. She studied at Oxford and lived in Britain with her husband and sons. In 1988 she came home to nurse her mother just as the 8888 Uprising broke out, and she became its voice.

She co-founded the National League for Democracy. The army put her under house arrest in 1989. Her party won the 1990 election by a landslide, and the generals ignored it. Her calm defiance won world fame and the Nobel Prize.

Freed in 2010, she entered parliament and her party won the 2015 election. As State Counsellor she shared power with the army, and lost much of her standing abroad by defending it over the Rohingya exodus. In the 2021 coup the army arrested her again and courts gave her long prison terms.
sum: The leader of the democracy movement in Burma, winner of the Nobel Peace Prize in 1991, who spent about fifteen years under house arrest and later led the country's government.
